en: a noble girl can only pick flowers, play piano
and dress hair.
I took her in knowing that, but...
note: Trails off as in the source; msg ends here.

en: I wonder what my wife finds so objectionable
note: Follows #4722 on a new line in msgs 185169/185886, then a '...' fragment, so no end punctuation. Subject inferred: Mrs. Stanberg (cf. #4708, #4714).

en: Why does Stuart shun carrying on the house
note: Subject inferred: Stuart (the would-be writer, cf. #4728).

en: so stubbornly...
I can't believe wanting to be a writer is his only reason.
What is Stuart so torn about, I wonder?
It seems he wants to become a writer.
He's still going on about that?!
Even without working at some job,
he can live perfectly well, can't he?
No, carrying on this house
is the most important job there is!
Now, whatever it takes,
I must have Stuart get married.
To uphold the Stanberg family traditions,
I need Stuart
to get married.
Unless I see Stuart wed
and blessed with a child,
my duty will remain unfulfilled.
Upholding the Stanberg family traditions
and praying for its glory and prosperity:
that is my most important duty.
I am the master of this house,
Stanberg, the 13th of my line.
The 13th?
If you are not from Calstatt,
you can hardly be expected to know.
Our family has governed Calstatt
since more than 300 years ago,
a house of distinguished lineage.
Upholding the Stanberg family traditions
is my most important duty.
What brings you here in the dead of night?
So you can finally take it easy, eh?
note: Night scene: stern player register (the vampire protagonist).

en: Stuart is to be the 14th head;
when will you pass the headship on?
Probably once the wedding is over.
Well, before long.
Which means you'll soon be of no use.
On the worthless job of guarding a house
you spent most of your life, and now even
that job is about to be taken from you.
For the likes of you, I've brought a new job
note: No used_in (4765-4783): assumed to continue msg 185454 (player vampirizes Lord Stanberg).

en: as a favor. Rejoice.
Become a "Dhampir,"
and guard not your house, but me.
You...
Don't tell me...
note: Base: Lord Stanberg after #4769 (no used_in). Margarete msg 214539 gets a variant: name is the subject, #983 is '' there.

en: ...That's right.
S-
Stop it!
K-
Keep away from me!
I'll be tainted!
Are you saying that being drained by me
is the same as having your bloodline tainted?
Now this is amusing.
That makes you all the more worth draining.
Don't touch me!
Let go!
Aaaaagh!
For such a noble bloodline, you don't taste good.
I thought you'd be a little tastier than that.
And how will your wife take it?
note: Polite counterpart of #4705 'And what of your wife?'.

en: What happened? Was there a quarrel?
It's quite a mess in here.
You needn't tell me the rest.
I believe he'd like to become a writer.
let us go for a night stroll.
Lately, strolling at night seems to have
become a habit of mine.
let us stroll the night streets together.
Good mornin' to you.
note: Shared by 4 Hugo msgs; in 189188 it follows {PLAYER_NAME} + #4813 (slice 060), which must end with a space or be punctuation ending in a space.

en: Are you out for a stroll too, then?
note: Also after #4816 'good evening' (msg 189213); no time word, so it fits both.

en: (Something like that)
(No, I'm too busy for strolls)
Yes, something like that.
